gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named, dated measurement of what an SSD actually delivers on a 10Gbps link compared with a 5Gbps link. ssd-tester.com (Markus, tested 2026-07-08) measured 1,048 MB/s read and 1,025 MB/s write on a 10Gbps UGREEN path. Binary Tides (Silver Moon) measured about 398–401 MB/s read and 360 MB/s write on a 5Gbps USB 3.0 link. No reviewer we could find has published a measurement taken through any of the candidate switches themselves.
standout_why: I compared against the cited us.ugreen.com CM691 page (UGREEN's US store returned HTTP 429 to both WebFetch and storecheck, so I could not read it today), digitaldesksolutions.com (2026-10-28), techradar.com (only the title loaded) and the manuals.plus/Newegg listings. Digital Desk Solutions already gives the 5Gbps vs 10Gbps gap, but only as theory ('Roughly 500 MB/s' vs 'Roughly 1 GB/s'), and it says 'Nobody on the team used or measured these units.' None of the rivals gives a named lab's measured MB/s. None has a measurement through a switch either, and nobody else does. So our page can add measured numbers in place of rounded theory, but it cannot add a benchmark of a switch.
decides: This supports the 10Gbps pick (UGREEN CM691 / Cable Matters 201160) over the 5Gbps budget switches. Measured 5Gbps throughput (about 400 MB/s read) is roughly 2.6× below measured 10Gbps throughput (about 1,048 MB/s read). The two tests used different drives (SATA MX500 vs an NVMe enclosure), so the ratio describes each link class and not one drive. It also weakens ChatGPT's line that a 5Gbps switch is 'fine' for a SATA SSD: in Binary Tides' test, a SATA MX500 on a 5Gbps link read about 400 MB/s. The finding does not pick between the 10Gbps candidates, because nobody has measured them.

findings.note: Measured by ssd-tester.com (author 'Markus'); the page says the test was run on 08 July 2026. The interface is listed as USB 3.2 Gen 2x1 (10 Gbit/s). The SSD and host are not named on this page. This is a direct connection to an enclosure, not through a switch. It is the measured ceiling a 10Gbps switch such as the CM691 could pass on.

The drives differ (SATA vs NVMe), so this compares link classes, not one drive.
